habitat: Singly or in pairs in well-developed riverine forest, coastal and lowland forest, and thickets on moist, rocky hillsides. It forages on the ground and in the mid-stratum.
summary: A fairly common resident. The underparts and underwings are bright yellow. The eyes are reddish, with conspicuous white eyelids. The identification line says the head is grey and the rest is olive-brown. The description says the upper parts are olive-green. The immature’s crown is the same colour as the back. The call is a loud nasal pur, pur, pur, pur, peh, peh, peh, peh, peh. The Kemp paper name Yellowbellied Bulbul and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Sombre Greenbul is a plainer olive bird with a creamy-white eye. Yellow-bellied Greenbul has bright yellow underparts and underwings.

viewNotes.note: Bright yellow underparts, reddish eye and a white eyelid. The upper parts are olive-brown on the identification line and olive-green in the description.
Yellow throat and breast, reddish eye and white eyelid.
The upper-part colour conflicts between olive-brown and olive-green.
A flight pattern of the upperwing was not described.
The crown matches the back. Newman does not name that colour.

calls.description: A loud nasal pur, pur, pur, pur, peh, peh, peh, peh, peh, often from several birds at once. Grade A call from Lower Imenti Forest, Meru County, Kenya. Grade A recordings from Namibia are ND. The filename is XC1072510-550257281.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The upper parts are olive-brown on the identification line and olive-green in the description, so no back colour is stored. The grade A call is from Kenya. Namibian grade A recordings are ND. No flight photograph was found. Population figures and the Kemp name Yellowbellied Bulbul were left unchanged.
